_comment: C0 body translation · nightfall (2026-11-06). Key contract per cursor.en.json; sources/related counts must match the source file.

axes.model_access: No model picking is offered: the detection engine is the vendor's own, the official pages disclose no model tiers and give no bring-your-own-model entry point. What it guards is your agent and LLM chain — the DLP API takes text and files, the MCP Gateway sits between "your AI clients and remote MCP servers", and the Inference Hooks documentation pages name Cursor, Claude Code and VS Code Copilot. Whether the detection model can be replaced or chosen: no official statement captured, recorded as unknown.
axes.runtime: Hosted delivery: scanning goes through the /v3/scan and /v3/upload endpoints on the API side, with results reviewed in the console and on the Violations page (on record in the release notes). There is a local agent on the endpoint side — the macOS/Windows endpoint agent appears in the docs and release notes (AirDrop and Bluetooth exfiltration control, MDM-granted permissions) — but detection and verdicts remain a service-side capability per the official framing. A self-hosted or air-gapped form: absent from the pages captured, recorded as unknown.
axes.local_files: What you can hand it (official FAQ on record): "plain text, structured and unstructured files, and even images", with JSON, XML and CSV named; on the endpoint side the agent reads files on your machine in order to block at the moment of read. **Whether submitted content is retained, and for how long**: not declared in the DLP API docs or FAQ, moved to unknowns. File and image capability limits live on the supported-file-types page (not read item by item in this pass).
axes.background: The asynchronous surface is explicit: file scanning is a multi-step flow — /v3/upload (POST to start), /v3/upload/{fileId} (PATCH chunks), /finish, then /scan — with webhook and asynchronous-notification pages on record, and events aggregated in the console. **This layer runs vendor-side**, so the "keeps running after shutdown" local-task semantic does not apply.
axes.tools: API surface (on record in the DLP docs): request fields payload, policyUUIDs, detectionRules, redactionConfig and alertConfig; response fields findings, redactedPayload and message. Extension surface: an official Nightfall MCP server documentation page (letting AI assistants query your security data directly), Inference Hooks into IDEs and agents, and Premier-tier OpenTelemetry audit trail plus MCP server discovery (on the pricing page). MCP transport details and tool-approval semantics: not verified item by item in this pass.
axes.context: Its "context" is policy and rule set, not conversation memory: one scan is defined by which rules run, via policyUUIDs and detectionRules. The revisable history has a stated boundary — MCP Gateway audit records carry user, server, tool, status and request payload, with payloads "capped at 8 KiB"; how anything beyond that is handled is not stated officially, recorded as unknown.
axes.permissions: Clause by clause with sources: SOC 2 Type 2 is on record at the security page; **transfer path, retention period and training use of customer content have no itemised answer on any official page captured in this pass** (neither the developer-api docs nor the FAQ declares it, and /trust returned 404), so all three go to unknowns with no inference such as "not used for training". Tier and quota facts (pricing page, no prices): Foundation Edition covers "Data Detection & Response across 12 API-integrated SaaS apps", the endpoint agent "covers every SaaS app, desktop app, and AI app", each user licence includes "2 endpoint devices", and every plan includes "150 GB of data-at-rest scanning"; Premier adds the AI agent stack, MCP server discovery and the OpenTelemetry audit trail. Red line: what is on record are detection categories and actions (block, mask/redact, removeFinding, cryptoConfig); this site publishes no detection or miss rate and does not rank Nightfall against self-deployed options — the selection question is whether your data may leave your boundary.
axes.fit: Fits: SaaS, endpoint and agent surfaces already in use and needing one control plane; needing real actions at the MCP and IDE-hook layer; happy to use a hosted API to strip PII and credentials before data reaches a model; wanting an events and audit surface rather than building one. Not a fit: a hard "text never leaves my boundary" constraint, or a requirement for an auditable open-source licence (that constraint points at self-deployed tooling); teams that only need leaked-credential detection with an incident workflow.

runs:
**This site has not run it end to end**: no /v3/scan call, no MCP Gateway or endpoint agent deployed, so no detection rate, miss rate, latency or ranking is produced. This archive only organises statements on record at the site, the Security page, the Pricing page, the help-centre home, two developer-api pages, the MCP Gateway doc and the release notes.

**Suggested measurements** (four):

- **What happens to payloads beyond 8 KiB** (the Gateway audit boundary is on record; over-limit behaviour is not)
- **Restore and audit semantics when redactionConfig meets cryptoConfig**
- **Whether content handed to the API is retained vendor-side, and for how long** (not on record; a due-diligence must-ask)
- **Latency and offline availability between the endpoint agent and hosted verdicts** (the macOS blocking actions are on record; chain behaviour is not)
unknowns:
- Transfer path, retention period and training use of customer content (no itemised official answer captured)
- ISO 27001, GDPR/DPA, subprocessor list and pen-test report access (/trust returned 404)
- Whether a self-hosted or air-gapped form exists
- Whether the underlying detection model can be replaced or chosen
- How the MCP Gateway handles payloads above 8 KiB
- Endpoint agent offline availability and latency behaviour
- Per-tier rate/quota ceilings and overage handling (the pricing page gives coverage facts only)
- Mainland-network direct reachability and filing status (not measured, not searched)
related: Two sides of the same constraint: that archive keeps recognition and operators inside your boundary, this one hands detection and verdicts to a hosted API.
A different object class: that archive's main axis is leaked credentials and the incident loop, this one's is PII/source code and agent data movement.
The vendor publishes Inference Hooks for IDE/agent surfaces, and the documentation pages name Claude Code among those entry points.
